methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Travis Kalanick that has raised $1.7B to date. The comparable universe consists of 8 private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing (including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) and 1 public comparable, though the sector remains fragmented and early-stage weighted.

Given the scarcity of same-stage, same-tier peers in the robotics sector—zero qualifying matches across narrow Growth-stage filters—the Peer-Median method is not applicable. Instead, Stage-Progression analysis anchors the valuation. Using total capital raised ($1.7B) as a proxy baseline, a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage progression yields $2.0B. This reflects the company's progression beyond its funding base but remains conservative absent richer comparables data.

The triangulated range is $1.7B (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $2.0B supported by a single methodology. The primary uncertainty is the limited applicability of peer-based cross-checks; a fuller robotics comps set—particularly private companies at the Growth stage and recent funding milestones—would tighten confidence. Near-term fundraising outcomes and margin progression in the underlying robotics vertical will be critical to validating whether valuations move toward the upper or lower bound of this range.
